* Bindings

** SWIG

Every binding's wrappers are generated with a SWIG fork, [[https://github.com/jordanschupbach/swig][jordanschupbach/swig]], pinned as
the ~swig~ flake input and on ~PATH~ as ~swig~ in every dev shell. The JavaScript binding uses its
Node-API backend (~-javascript -napi~).

- ~just update-swig~ bumps the pinned fork revision in ~flake.lock~.
- To use a local checkout, ~export DATAMUNGE_SWIG_SRC=$HOME/projects/swig~ (e.g. in
  ~.envrc.local~). Both direnv and the ~just~ recipes then pass ~--override-input swig~.

using System;
using System.Diagnostics;
using System.Collections.Generic;

// NOTE: if using repl, uncomment the following line to load the datamungedotnet.dll
// and then recomment it back when compiling as a standalone program
// #r "src/datamungedotnet/bin/Debug/net10.0/datamungedotnet.dll"

class stl_ex {
  static void Main() {
    Console.WriteLine("Hello, World!");

    var v = new DVector();
    for(uint i=0; i<10; i++) {
      v.Add(((double)i)*1.1);
    }
    for(uint i=0; i<v.Count; i++) {
      Console.WriteLine(v[(int)i]);
    }

    var v2 = new IVector();
    for(uint i=0; i<10; i++) {
      v2.Add((int)(i*2));
    }
    for(uint i=0; i<v2.Count; i++) {
      Console.WriteLine(v2[(int)i]);
    }

    var p = new DPair(3.14, 2.71);
    Console.WriteLine(p.first);
    Console.WriteLine(p.second);

    var p2 = new IPair(42, 7);
    Console.WriteLine(p2.first);

  }
}

** D (~examples/d/source/app.d~)

#+begin_src d
module app;

import std.stdio : writeln;
import datamunge;

class TimesTwo : Callback {
  override double call(double x) {
    return x * 2.0;
  }
}

void main() {
  hello();

  auto vec = make_dvector(1.0, 2.0, 3.0);
  writeln("sum_dvector(1,2,3) = ", sum_dvector(vec));

  auto pair = make_dpair(4.0, 5.0);
  writeln("sum_dpair(4,5) = ", sum_dpair(pair));

  auto cb = new TimesTwo();
  writeln("call_with_callback(3.0) = ", call_with_callback(3.0, cb));
  auto vec2 = map_dvector_with_callback(vec, cb);
  writeln("sum_dvector(map_dvector_with_callback(1,2,3)) = ", sum_dvector(vec2));
}
#+end_src

** Go (~examples/go/datamunge_ex.go~)

#+begin_src go :results output :exports both
package main

import (
	"datamunge"
	"fmt"
)

func main() {
	if err := datamunge.Hello(); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}

	v := datamunge.Must(datamunge.MakeDvector(1.0, 2.0, 3.0))
	fmt.Printf("sum_dvector:\t%v\n", datamunge.Must(datamunge.SumDvector(v)))

	p := datamunge.Must(datamunge.MakeDpair(1.25, 2.75))
	fmt.Printf("sum_dpair:\t%v\n", datamunge.Must(datamunge.SumDpair(p)))

	cb := datamunge.Must(datamunge.NewCallback())
	defer cb.Close()
	fmt.Printf("call_with_callback(3.0):\t%v\n", datamunge.Must(datamunge.CallWithCallback(3.0, cb)))
}
#+end_src

** Java (~examples/java/DatamungeEx.java~)

#+begin_src java :results output :exports both
import datamunge.Callback;
import datamunge.Datamunge;

public class DatamungeEx {
  // A Java subclass overrides the C++ Callback's virtual call().
  static class TimesTwo extends Callback {
    @Override
    public double call(double x) {
      return 2.0 * x;
    }
  }

  public static void main(String[] args) {
    Datamunge.hello();
    var pair = Datamunge.makeDpair(1.0, 2.0); // std::pair<double, double> is the Pair record
    System.out.println("make_dpair: " + pair + ", sum_dpair = " + Datamunge.sumDpair(pair));
    try (var cb = new TimesTwo()) {
      System.out.println("call_with_callback(3.0) = " + Datamunge.callWithCallback(3.0, cb));
    }
  }
}
#+end_src

#+RESULTS:

** JavaScript (~examples/javascript/datamunge_ex.js~)

#+begin_src js :results output :exports both
// Local dev: build first (`just build-javascript`), then run this example.
const datamunge = require("../../index.js");

datamunge.hello();

// Note: SWIG's Node/JavaScript backend does not support directors/virtual-method
// overrides the same way as Python/Ruby/Perl. `Callback` can still be passed,
// but the default implementation is identity.
const cb = new datamunge.Callback();
console.log("call_with_callback(3.0) =", datamunge.call_with_callback(3.0, cb));
const v2 = datamunge.map_dvector_with_callback(datamunge.make_dvector(1.0, 2.0, 3.0), cb);
console.log("sum_dvector(map_dvector_with_callback) =", datamunge.sum_dvector(v2));

// Bridging: pass a JS function into native code (via C callback trampoline).
console.log("call_with_function(3.0) =", datamunge.call_with_function(3.0, (x) => x * 2.0));
const out = datamunge.map_array_with_function([1.0, 2.0, 3.0], (x) => x * 2.0);
console.log("map_array_with_function([1,2,3]) =", out);
#+end_src

** OCaml (~examples/ocaml/datamunge_ex.ml~)

#+begin_src ocaml :results output :exports both
#use "topfind";;
#require "datamunge";;
open Datamunge

let () =
  hello ();
  let v = make_dvector 1.0 2.0 3.0 in
  Printf.printf "sum_dvector:\t%g\n" (sum_dvector v);
  let p = make_dpair 1.25 2.75 in
  Printf.printf "sum_dpair:\t%g\n" (sum_dpair p);
  (* An OCaml subclass overrides the C++ Callback's virtual call(). *)
  let cb = Callback.extend ~call:(fun _ x -> 2.0 *. x) () in
  Printf.printf "call_with_callback(3.0):\t%g\n" (call_with_callback 3.0 cb);
  let v2 = map_dvector_with_callback (make_dvector 1.0 2.0 3.0) cb in
  Printf.printf "sum_dvector(map_dvector_with_callback(1,2,3)):\t%g\n" (sum_dvector v2)

** Perl (~examples/perl/datamunge_ex.pl~)

#+begin_src perl :results output :exports both
use strict;
use warnings;

use Datamunge;

Datamunge::hello();

my $dp = Datamunge::DPair->new(1.0, 2.0);
print "DPair: First=" . $dp->swig_first_get() . ", Second=" . $dp->swig_second_get() . "\n";

{
  package TimesTwo;
  our @ISA = ('Datamunge::Callback');

  sub call {
    my ($self, $x) = @_;
    return $x * 2.0;
  }
}

my $cb = TimesTwo->new();
print "call_with_callback(3.0) = ", Datamunge::call_with_callback(3.0, $cb), "\n";
my $v = Datamunge::make_dvector(1.0, 2.0, 3.0);
my $v2 = Datamunge::map_dvector_with_callback($v, $cb);
print "sum_dvector(map_dvector_with_callback(1,2,3)) = ", Datamunge::sum_dvector($v2), "\n";
#+end_src

library(datamunger)

#+begin_src ruby :results output :exports both
require "datamunge"

Datamunge.hello

pair = Datamunge.make_dpair(1.0, 2.0)  # std::pair<double, double> is a two-element Array
puts "make_dpair: #{pair.inspect}, sum_dpair = #{Datamunge.sum_dpair(pair)}"

# A Ruby subclass overrides the C++ Callback's virtual call().
class TimesTwo < Datamunge::Callback
  def call(x) = x * 2.0
end

cb = TimesTwo.new
puts "call_with_callback(3.0) = #{Datamunge.call_with_callback(3.0, cb)}"
v = Datamunge.make_dvector(1.0, 2.0, 3.0)
v2 = Datamunge.map_dvector_with_callback(v, cb)
puts "sum_dvector(map_dvector_with_callback(1,2,3)) = #{Datamunge.sum_dvector(v2)}"
#+end_src

#+begin_src tcl :results output :exports both
package require datamunge

datamunge::hello

set pair [datamunge::make_dpair 1.0 2.0]  ;# std::pair<double, double> is a two-element list
puts "make_dpair: $pair, sum_dpair = [datamunge::sum_dpair $pair]"

# A TclOO subclass overrides the C++ Callback's virtual call().
oo::class create TimesTwo {
    superclass ::datamunge::Callback
    method call {x} { expr {2.0 * $x} }
}
set cb [TimesTwo new]
puts "call_with_callback(3.0) = [datamunge::call_with_callback 3.0 $cb]"
set v [datamunge::make_dvector 1.0 2.0 3.0]
set v2 [datamunge::map_dvector_with_callback $v $cb]
puts "sum_dvector(map_dvector_with_callback(1,2,3)) = [datamunge::sum_dvector $v2]"
